content.user_title: Trace Images to Their Earliest Known Source
content.value_statement: Reverse image results often confuse similarity with provenance and can expose sensitive material. This skill guides multi-engine searches, preprocessing, source validation, and responsible confidence grading.
actual_capabilities: Selects suitable reverse image engines for faces, products, text, landmarks, regional content, and exact duplicates.
Guides full-frame, cropped, mirrored, enhanced, and keyframe searches across multiple engines.
Provides reproducible ImageMagick, FFmpeg, ExifTool, Tesseract, and hashing examples for media preparation.
Explains how to validate publication dates, page context, archive captures, filenames, credits, and image resolution.
Separates exact matches from visual similarity and grades results as confirmed, probable, match only, or unconfirmed.
Documents privacy, consent, biometric, and false-positive concerns for face searches and sensitive images.
limitations: Search engines have incomplete indexes, changing results, regional restrictions, and login barriers.
The earliest indexed copy may not be the true first publication.
Face matches and visually similar images require independent corroboration.
Uploading an image shares it with external services and may be unsuitable for confidential material.

use_cases.title: Verify Breaking News Images
use_cases.description: Trace a circulating image to earlier publications and test whether its current caption is accurate.

use_cases.title: Investigate Suspicious Profiles
use_cases.description: Check whether a profile or listing image is stock, reused, or associated with unrelated identities.

use_cases.title: Trace Product and Brand Images
use_cases.description: Find earlier product photographs, modified copies, watermarks, and likely licensing sources.

prompt_templates.title: Search One Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the earliest known source for [image]. Search at least three suitable engines, separate exact matches from similar images, and report confidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has one image and needs a structured provenance search.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Reused Profile Photo
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether [profile image] is reused, stock, or linked to unrelated identities. Respect consent limits and treat face-engine results as unconfirmed leads.
prompt_templates.scenario: A fraud analyst needs to assess a suspicious profile image.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Video Through Keyframes
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract representative keyframes from [video], search distinctive frames and crops, compare dates, and identify the earliest corroborated publication without overstating null results.
prompt_templates.scenario: A researcher needs to trace a reposted or miscaptioned video.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Auditable Provenance Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an evidence log for [media]. Record every engine, transformation, result, source date, archive check, contradiction, privacy decision, and final confidence grade.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced investigator needs a reproducible report suitable for review.

output_examples.input: A product photo from a suspicious marketplace listing.
output: Evidence: TinEye found an older, larger copy on a supplier page, while Lens found several later listings.
Caveat: The supplier page is the earliest indexed source, not proven authorship.

output_examples.input: A social post claims that a protest image was taken today.
output: Evidence: The same image appeared in an archived news gallery three years earlier with matching pixel details.
Conclusion: The current caption is false about the date, but the image itself is not proven fabricated.

output_examples.input: A short video has no direct reverse image matches.
output: Assessment: Match only from a keyframe crop.
Evidence: A storefront crop matches an older article, but the full video remains unverified.
Next step: Corroborate the location, publication date, and relationship between the article image and the video.

best_practices: Preserve and hash the original before creating clearly named derivatives.
Search multiple engines and record every query, transformation, result, and null.
Confirm candidate matches through page context, pixel details, dates, archives, and independent sources.
anti_patterns: Do not treat visual similarity or a face-engine score as identity proof.
Do not claim that no search result proves originality or authenticity.
Do not upload confidential or biometric images without authorization and a lawful basis.

faq.question: Does the skill automatically search every engine?
faq.answer: No. It provides a structured workflow, engine selection guidance, and preprocessing commands for an agent or investigator to follow.

faq.question: Can it prove who created an image?
faq.answer: Not by search results alone. It helps identify the earliest known publication and supporting evidence, which may still require attribution checks.

faq.question: What does a zero-result search mean?
faq.answer: It means the image was not found in the searched indexes. It does not prove that the image is original or authentic.

faq.question: Can it analyze video?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow extracts representative keyframes and searches them as still images, including distinctive crops.

faq.question: Is face search always appropriate?
faq.answer: No. Face search may involve biometric data, consent requirements, legal restrictions, service terms, and serious false-positive risks.

faq.question: How should sensitive images be handled?
faq.answer: Avoid external uploads when disclosure is unacceptable. Use authorized tools, remove unnecessary identifying details, and document the privacy decision.
